skill.name: error-memory
skill.description: Records concise project error lessons so agents can avoid repeating build, context, and requirement mistakes.
skill.summary: Creates a lightweight project error memory for repeated agent mistakes.
skill.author: Aceek

security_audit.summary: All static command-execution findings are false positives caused by markdown inline code and code fences. The skill has one low-severity semantic concern because it instructs agents to create or append a project-local memory file.

remediation.issue: Project file writes are described without an explicit consent step.
remediation.suggestion: Add a rule to ask before creating or updating `.claude/errors.md`, especially in clean or read-only repositories.

remediation.issue: Error records may capture sensitive project context.
remediation.suggestion: Tell agents to omit secrets, credentials, customer data, and private incident details from error entries.

semantic_findings.title: Implicit Project File Modification
semantic_findings.description: The skill instructs agents to append to `.claude/errors.md` and create it if missing. This can alter project files and store project-specific error history without an explicit confirmation step.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: Lines 33 and 38 directly instruct appending to or creating the file. The risk is limited because the file is local markdown and no network or command execution is shown.

content.value_statement: Teams lose time when agents repeat the same project mistakes. This skill records concise error lessons in a shared project file.
actual_capabilities: Classifies mistakes as technical, context, or comprehension errors.
Guides root-cause analysis for build failures and requirement misses.
Defines a one-line format for project error records.
Provides a template for `.claude/errors.md` when it is missing.
Encourages checking previous errors before new project work.
limitations: It does not run tests or verify fixes by itself.
It depends on the agent to record accurate root causes.
It can add project files when followed without user confirmation.
It does not synchronize records across repositories.

use_cases.title: Prevent Repeated Build Mistakes
use_cases.description: Record a failed build, its root cause, and the rule that prevents the same error later.

use_cases.title: Capture Project Conventions
use_cases.description: Document missed naming, structure, or framework conventions after a correction from a user.

use_cases.title: Review Correction History
use_cases.description: Scan past mistakes before assigning similar work or reviewing repeated agent behavior.

prompt_templates.title: Record a Simple Error
prompt_templates.prompt: Use error-memory to record the mistake I just made, the root cause, and the rule I should follow next time.

prompt_templates.title: Classify a Failed Change
prompt_templates.scenario: Categorize a build, context, or comprehension issue
prompt_templates.prompt: Classify this failure with error-memory, then write a short lesson that prevents the same issue in this project.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Reusable Lesson
prompt_templates.scenario: Turn a user correction into a durable rule
prompt_templates.prompt: Use error-memory to convert this user correction into a reusable project rule with a clear cause and fix.

prompt_templates.title: Audit Recurring Mistakes
prompt_templates.prompt: Review the recent error-memory entries, identify repeated root causes, and propose three rules to reduce future failures.

output_examples.input: A test failed because I used the wrong import path.
output_examples.output: Adds a technical lesson that names the mistaken import assumption and the rule for checking local module paths first.

output_examples.input: The user corrected a UI convention I missed.
output_examples.output: Adds a context lesson describing the missed convention and the exact rule to apply before editing similar files.

output_examples.input: I misunderstood the requested feature scope.
output_examples.output: Adds a comprehension lesson that states the missed requirement and the rule for confirming scope before implementation.

best_practices: Confirm that the recorded lesson does not include secrets or private customer data.
Keep each error entry short enough to scan before new work.
Review existing entries before changing tests, build files, or established patterns.
anti_patterns: Do not record blame, excuses, or long incident narratives.
Do not write sensitive project details into shared memory files.
Do not let old lessons override newer user instructions or repository policy.

faq.question: Does this skill execute commands?
faq.answer: No. The skill text describes a markdown process, but it may guide an agent to edit a project file.

faq.question: Where are lessons stored?
faq.answer: The skill directs agents to use `.claude/errors.md` in the current project.

faq.question: What types of errors can it record?
faq.answer: It supports technical errors, missed project context, and misunderstood requirements.

faq.question: Can Codex or Claude Code use it?
faq.answer: Yes. The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Should it store sensitive details?
faq.answer: No. Error notes should omit secrets, credentials, customer data, and private incident details.

faq.question: Does it replace tests or review?
faq.answer: No. It helps remember lessons, but tests and human review still verify the work.
